alex: Heads-up — seeing a tail spike in token-level latency for streaming on prod-gpu around 22:40 UTC. Chunk cadence is noisy: lots of tiny chunks then multi-second stall. Attaching quick flame/profile snapshot (small).

maria: ugh. any correlation with kernel swaps or kv-evictions?

ravi: I glanced at kernel logs — we did a kernel hotswap on the affected hosts due to a memory threshold breach at 22:39:58. Fallback to slower attention kernel for ~45s.

sasha: do we have per-route token breakdowns for that timeframe? want to see if a single customer route caused small batches.

alex: yes — pulled per-route token latency (token_p50/p95/p99) for 22:30-23:00. Route /chat-widget-1 shows p99 jump from 180ms -> 1.8s. Others stable.

infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-478 (auto). Hosts: gpu-pool-7a.[3-5]. Kernel fallback event count: 3. KV eviction pressure: medium.

maria: stack from the host where fallback happened (short):
```
# kernel decision snippet
if (free_mem < kernel_switch_threshold && batch_len < min_batch_for_fast_kernel) {
  select(kernel: ATTENTION_FUSED_SLOW);
} else {
  select(kernel: ATTENTION_FUSED_FAST);
}
```

maria: the heuristic checks both free mem and current batch length. small bursts + memory pressure => slower kernel.

ravi: streaming batching heuristic currently uses a 25ms emission window + max_batch 64. but for chat-widget-1 we saw many tiny user messages that kept creating emit events <10 tokens -> batch never hit min_batch_for_fast_kernel.

sasha: so two compounding factors: (1) tiny per-request token counts preventing efficient batching, (2) memory pressure forcing kernel fallback. That explains the cadence: many tiny chunks with occasional heavy flushes and stalls.

alex: profiling shows token generation time split: compute 55%, scheduling/queue 20%, kv lookup 10%, kernel swap cost (cold) 15%. Kernel swap cost spikes during fallback windows.

joel: can you paste the PromQLs you used? want to add to the streaming dashboard.

alex: sure — two useful panels I used: 
1) token latency histogram per-route (P99 focus):
```
sum by (route, le) (increase(redwood_stream_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))
```
2) kernel fallback count:
```
sum(increase(redwood_runtime_kernel_fallback_total[1h])) by (host)
```
3) chunk emission cadence (emit per-second):
```
rate(redwood_stream_chunk_emitted_total[1m])
```

maria: added a quick chart in the livetail dashboard for kernel_fallback_total and kv_evictions.

ravi: quick mitigation ideas: 
- temporarily relax kernel_switch_threshold on affected hosts to avoid fallback during transient mem blips
- increase batching window to 50ms for low-token routes (adaptive per-route window)
- increase KV hotset size / reduce eviction aggressiveness for high-throughput routes

sasha: long term: we should make kernel selection cost-aware instead of binary threshold. i.e., if expected per-token cost on fast kernel with small batch < slow kernel cost, pick fast even if memory tight. Need a microcost model.

alex: agreed. immediate next steps:
- mariA to push KV eviction metrics to per-route dashboard (maria) — ACTION 1
- ravi to toggle kernel threshold on gpu-pool-7a for 2hrs and watch (ravi) — ACTION 2
- sasha to prototype adaptive batch window per-route (PR branch: feature/adaptive-window) — ACTION 3
- joel to add token-level p99 overlay on streaming dashboard for quick alerting (joel) — ACTION 4

maria: ACTION 1: done (added panel, filtering by route).

ravi: ACTION 2: toggled threshold at 23:05 UTC on gpu-pool-7a to relaxed. early signal: kernel_fallback_total dropped to 0 for those hosts but avg memory used stayed same. monitoring for regressions.

alex: good. ravi — please keep an eye on cost impact (if fast kernel uses more VRAM leading to OOM).

ravi: noted. no OOMs yet.

sasha: started a small prototype for adaptive-window. initial idea: if recent batch sizes < B_min for route X, slowly increase emit window up to W_max until effective batch grows. will PR tomorrow.

joel: added p99 overlay + simple alert rule: if route p99 > 1s and kernel_fallback_total > 0 for 5m -> page on-call.

alex: follow-up: need a small perf test to reproduce micro pattern: many tiny incoming messages with KV hits/evictions toggled. i'll try to craft a replay load.

maria: can also toggle KV hotset size on staging to run the same replay.

ravi: re: metrics instrumentation, we should record kernel selection decision metadata per-request (kernel_chosen, batch_size_at_choice, mem_headroom) so dashboards can surface decision heatmaps.

sasha: +1. that will help build the microcost model too.

alex: ok creating ticket ENGRT-3109 with summary + actions, linking logs and graphs (<https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ENGRT-3109>).

infra-bot: Ticket ENGRT-3109 created by alex. Priority: P2.

joel: thanks everyone. keep updates in the ticket. :thumbsup:

alex: closing thread here — will post replay results in ENGRT-3109. :eyes:
